annotation.kind: source-faithful execution-level formulation of the residual bound in Lemma 3.2

assumptions: R is a real nonsingular upper triangular n-by-n matrix.
Every row system q_i^T R = x_i^T is computed by the displayed rounded forward-substitution recurrence applied to R transpose under the standard relative-error model.
xNorm denotes the nonnegative spectral norm of X.
P26RowPerturbationsControlled states exactly the norm implication obtained in equations (3.25)-(3.28) after a componentwise triangular-solve perturbation has been constructed.
The supplied Frobenius bound for the computed Q is equation (3.39), the consequence of Lemma 3.1 used by the source proof.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P26 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P26 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p26_t1_lemma_3_2 (fp : P26FPModel) (m n : Nat) (X : P26Matrix m n) (R : P26Matrix n n) (xNorm : Real) ... : p26FrobNorm (p26Residual (p26RoundedQ fp X R) R X) <= 2 * (n : Real)^2 * fp.u * xNorm
formal_statement.plain_language: For the matrix Q computed by rounded triangular row solves, the shifted-CholeskyQR residual has Frobenius norm at most 2 n squared u times the spectral norm of X.

informal_proof: Apply the triangular-solve backward-error result to each computed row, use equations (3.25)-(3.28) to bound that row's residual, aggregate the squared row bounds into the Frobenius norm, and use the Frobenius bound from Lemma 3.1 to obtain the constant 2.
informal_statement: Lemma 3.2 in the equivalent multiplication form (3.40): the computed shifted-CholeskyQR factors have residual at most 2 n^2 u times the spectral norm of X.

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The one substantial importable result is the complete forward-substitution backward-error theorem, applied to the transposed upper-triangular row solves. It constructs the perturbation matrix with the sharp gamma_n componentwise bound and exact perturbed system. The private N construction rebuilds the rounding-product, subtraction-fold, and triangular-solve analysis; the L construction invokes that theorem once. Frobenius aggregation and the paper-specific constants are shared supporting work, and Mathlib has no floating-point triangular-solve theorem.
